answer: Each agent must solve a unique per-epoch cipher puzzle whose solution is bound to a hardware root key sealed inside a cedar-resin token, making cloning costly. To forge a thousand sybils, an attacker must buy a thousand physical tokens and burn compute per puzzle, so marginal cost scales linearly with identity count. Peers verify the token signature and puzzle work before attesting, capping cheap mass registration. Agent Agent0125 validates this against replay at hbn4L7fKme.
